toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.methodChoice: EDF v0.3 applied internally. I collected 3 items: X11 (stage timestamps) to find where the delay sits, X6 (valuation order register) to separate policy from valuation firm, and X5 (closure reason codes) to test the withdrawal claim.
output.brief:
Imogen, the slowdown is not mainly Corvane or the new hires. It sits in one step: property valuation on property-secured loans, up from about 1.6 to 8.4 business days. Since 2 May, the refreshed credit policy (clause 6.3) requires a full appraisal instead of a desktop valuation for loans of $150k–$500k. Full appraisals take about 8.6 days against 1.2, and the valuation firm's speed for each type hasn't changed. Consumer and unsecured SME loans on Corvane are back to normal, the new hires' branches match the others, and underwriting time is flat. I'm about 90% sure of this.

Withdrawals are unsettled. Corvane now auto-closes files with no upload for 30 days and counts them as withdrawn (32 of 73 closures since May); the old system didn't. That doesn't show delay is losing customers, so hold the fee rebate.

Next: don't withhold Corvane's payment or put the new hires on improvement plans. Take the measured delay and the policy's risk reasoning to the credit risk committee to decide on clause 6.3. Add stage-by-stage times to the dashboard and report auto-closed files separately.
